subject.title: feat(slack): support running as a real Slack user (user identity)

question: Should OpenClaw officially support an agent that reads and posts as an authorizing human Slack user across that user's visible conversations?
rationale: This is a new human-credential trust boundary and impersonation model, not merely a transport implementation detail; repository policy requires explicit ownership of its consent, scope, disclosure, and recovery behavior.

options.title: Approve after repair and proof
options.body: Accept the capability after the mixed-account defect is fixed and redacted live evidence demonstrates the documented Slack behavior and security boundaries.

options.title: Ship as guarded preview
options.body: Keep the mode explicitly experimental and advanced-only until broader live workspace experience establishes reliable event delivery and safe operator expectations.

options.title: Do not support human identity
options.body: Retain bot identity plus optional read-only user tokens and decline autonomous posting as a human account.

recommendation.title: Approve after repair and proof
recommendation.body: Accept the capability after the mixed-account defect is fixed and redacted live evidence demonstrates the documented Slack behavior and security boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person most directly to Slack provider startup, Socket Mode, diagnostics, and the proposed feature direction.
